title: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging
description: A logging abstraction for .NET applications with built-in console and debug providers.

data.text: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging provides a logging abstraction for .NET. It supports structured logging, log levels, and various logging providers including console, debug, EventSource, and third-party loggers like Serilog and NLog.

data.title: Using ILogger
data.content: Inject and use ILogger in a service.

terms.definition: The main interface for writing logs.
Severity levels: Trace, Debug, Information, Warning, Error, Critical.

data.title: Structured Logging
data.text: Use message templates with placeholders for structured logging: `LogInformation("User {UserId} logged in", userId)`.

The logging abstraction writes through `ILogger<T>`, and the provider is a configuration detail. The important discipline is to log structured values rather than formatted strings: `_logger.LogInformation("Order {OrderId} placed", id)` records `OrderId` as a named field that a log backend can filter and group on.

data.title: Structured logging without and with scope
Never interpolate values into the message
data.text: `logger.LogInformation("Order " + order.Id + " placed")` or `$"Order {order.Id} placed"` builds one opaque string, so the backend cannot filter by `OrderId` and each unique id creates a new message type. Always pass values as arguments to a template with named placeholders — that is the difference between logging and structured logging.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ILogger is the standard logging interface
Supports structured logging with message templates
data.takeaway: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging provides a consistent logging experience across .NET.
